comparator.sourceNotes: Current adopted2026–2027 AppendixArticles1–8,11 and current digital guide programme30401 govern this English joint TU Delft/Erasmus bachelor. Retained required current-entrant core:60ECYear1including the first formally listed representative programme-assigned mixed practical pairNB1430+NB1445(4ECeach),and60ECYear2. The alternative assignedpair isNB1435+NB1440; individual assignment is not a free student choice or a guaranteed allocation. CurrentNB2430is3EC; older-cohort transition4ECdoes not replace it. Year3contains30ECapprovedminor,20ECBEPand four2.5ECrestricted electives. A neutral representative spread walks the formal elective list in order,retaining the first suitable2.5ECoption for each unfilled five-weekoctal:NB3015(4B),NB3024(4A),thenNB3020(3A),NB3023(3B). Display uses chronological3A,3B,4A,4Border. One per octal is a planning choice,not an invented institutional rule. FormerNB3026/NB3014overlap4A;NB3026also has an actual lottery,not guaranteed access. NB3020expects molecularbiology supplied by the completedcore. NB3023recommends basic human genetics but requires neither that preparation nor priorR. NB3024names legacyNB2181/NB2191; Appendix11explicitly maps these to currentNB2410/NB2315,which are completed. NB3014is recommended,explicitly not mandatory,forNB3015. Brightspacecourse andOsirisexam registration and course-specific oral/presentation registration must be timely; no future administrative dates or individual admission guaranteed. Current3A/3B/4A/4Bevidence comes from course registration/exam text and octal contact arrays,not merely quarter metadata. Minor may be thematic,approvedindividual or exchange; short minors require supplementation to30EC. No minor subject invented. BEPrequires all60first-yearECplus at least60ECfromyears2/3,approvedsupervisor/group,registration/proposal/planning and committee. Erasmusprojects require access paperwork at least3weeks beforestart. A samegroup afterNB3030/honours requirespermission; neither is selected. CompletingYear2andminor beforeBEPsatisfies the published credit threshold. BEPis generally20weeksparttime and may be scheduled to student needs alongside electives. Published current-cohort pathway verified; not a forecast of an individual future timetable. Fullprogramme catalogue includes transition/honours/alternative entries; its65entries are not summed as the degree.

alternatives.label: Molecular biology & quantitative living systems
alternatives.concept: Investigate biomolecules, cells and living systems through laboratory biology, evolution, mathematical and computational modelling, and physical and chemical foundations. Molecular disease and drug mechanisms provide biological applications; specialist nanoscale measurement remains a limitation.
alternatives.labelReason: Seven molecular, physiological and drug-mechanism courses, one evolutionary-biology course, one neuroscience course, two physical/chemical foundations and twelve mathematical/computational courses, plus PPD, implement a quantitative living-systems curriculum. Physical foundations are substantive but do not imply a complete specialist Nanobiology formation.
progression: All four-course terms, actual offerings, earlier formal prerequisites, first-year PPD and advanced-course floor are checked against the sole current workbook. Core biology precedes advanced pathology/pharmacology; mathematical and programming foundations precede advanced methods. Probability and Machine Learning accompany one another under actual NONE prerequisites; relevant advisory preparation is considered without inventing a hard rule.

alternatives.label: Molecular disease mechanisms & quantitative biology
alternatives.concept: Prioritise molecular and cellular disease mechanisms, pharmacology, immunity and organ-system consequences, supported by laboratory biology and quantitative methods. Additional brain and perception foundations support biological function; physical, evolutionary and advanced algorithmic specialisation have less weight.
alternatives.labelReason: Molecular pathology, pharmacology, infection/immunity, organ-system disease and anatomy organise this alternative around biomedical explanation. Quantitative methods and neural function remain substantive supporting study; no nanomedical-device formation is claimed.
progression: All four-course terms, actual offerings, earlier formal prerequisites, first-year PPD and advanced-course floor are checked against the sole current workbook. Core biology precedes advanced pathology/pharmacology; mathematical and programming foundations precede advanced methods. Probability and Machine Learning accompany one another under actual NONE prerequisites; relevant advisory preparation is considered without inventing a hard rule.
alternatives.distinctness: Six courses / 45 EC differ in each direction. The closest programme uniquely includes two physical/chemical foundations, evolution, Algorithms and Data Structures, Advanced Algorithms and Neural Networks and Deep Learning. This disease programme uniquely includes Functional Anatomy, Infection and Immunity, Mechanisms of Disease, Introduction to Data Science, Introduction to Brain and Behavior, and Perception and Action. These implement a different biomedical/organism-level emphasis; retained data preparation supports that inquiry rather than padding the difference.

candidates.label: Molecular health, disease and medical research
Nanoscale biophysics, measurement and biomedical technology

selection.assessment: Two programmes make substantive academic responses to the evidenced molecular, laboratory, mathematical and physical investigation of living systems. The closest integrates actual evolution, physical/chemical foundations and pharmacology with core molecular/laboratory and advanced computational work; this repairs its former excessive general-computing/neural weight. The disease alternative is independently supported by its interest cluster and changes six courses/45EC in each direction, prioritising immunity, organ-system explanation and biological function. The remaining nanoscale measurement/biophysical-technology cluster was individually reconsidered using actual waves/materials/thermodynamics, chemical laboratories and evolutionary content. Physical foundations are already included in the closest; further environmental energy/resource/material courses do not implement a new organising inquiry into living-cell physical measurement and biomedical instruments. Merely relabelling shared foundations or assuming a specialised project would not establish a third coherent distinct programme. This is an academic composition finding,not an offering failure,degree-name equivalence rule or requirement to reproduce all specialist Delft courses.

blocks: DNA/heredity, gene expression, genomes and biotechnology provide an important molecular-genetic foundation. The external course adds detailed genetic experiments, repair/recombination and techniques.
Both directly study molecular/cellular biology. The external module also incorporates physical-cell content not fully offered by UCR.
Both study biomolecule chemistry and biological biochemical function. The complete external structural-biology syllabus is not asserted as covered.

Both involve practical molecular/biochemical techniques; UCR DNA, proteins, bacteria and bioinformatics laboratory work provides a substantive experimental relationship rather than nanoscale biophysics.

Molecular pathology, neoplasia, genetic variation and diagnostics supply an important cancer/genetic-mechanism relationship. Dedicated genomics platforms, breast-cancer biomarker pipelines and patient stratification are additional external scope.

Evolutionary genetics, variation/selection, speciation and evolutionary genomics/development supply an important evolutionary relationship. Detailed conserved embryological processes, model-organism structures and stem-cell applications are additional external scope.
UCR supplies calculus, differential equations and mathematical model analysis corresponding to introductory mathematical methods; no vector/matrix content is inferred for this course.
The current TER identifies Math 3 as combining former Analysis 3 and Linear Algebra. UCR directly implements its linear-algebra part; the analysis part remains broader.

Both teach numerical equation and differential-equation methods, stability and error analysis. The external elective additionally develops diffusion/heat PDE discretisation; identical full scope is not asserted.

The current TER identifies Math 2 as the successor to Analysis 2. UCR multidimensional calculus/differential equations provide a substantive advanced-analysis relationship, without asserting identical syllabus.

UCR explicitly studies Fourier series and transforms, differential equations and linear systems. These supply an important part of the external differential-equations/Fourier methods, without claiming an identical complete syllabus.
Both supply probability and statistics for quantitative scientific investigation.
Scientific computation and biological data methods

Regression/classification, statistical validation and unsupervised learning provide an important data-analysis part of bioinformatics. Genome assembly, sequence alignment, structural prediction and guaranteed biological datasets are additional external scope.

Filtering, segmentation, tracking and recognition pipelines provide substantive quantitative image-analysis methods. The external course additionally teaches advanced biological microscopy acquisition and experimental fluorescence techniques.
Both establish programming and computational problem-solving; UCR does not claim the external biomolecular programming assignments.
Both introduce neuroscience and brain function; the UCR course also studies evolution, animal cognition and research ethics.
Physical foundations, specialised external study, project and minor

Chemical bonds, reactions/equilibria, thermodynamics and polymer experiments provide actual chemical foundations. The external chemistry course adds carbon functional groups, stereochemistry and life-science analytical scope.

Waves, optical spectroscopy, material structure and stress/strain supply a substantive physical/optical foundation. Detailed Newtonian motion and ray-optical microscope formation extend beyond the documented UCR scope.

The external introductory disciplinary survey integrates nanobiological questions. Related foundations are present and credited in their own subject rows; no separate UCR nanobiology survey credit is invented.

General chemistry, waves and biological modelling provide preparation, but the external unit organises molecular mechanics, forces and biological physical models as a distinct inquiry; those specialised credits remain visible.

UCR has actual molecular wet-lab and physical/material experiments, but not this distinct programme-assigned biophysical techniques laboratory. Its credits are not replaced by generic laboratory experience.
Wave study supplies some physical preparation; a sustained electricity/magnetism and electromagnetic-field sequence is not established by the selected UCR content.

Programming, numerical analysis, linear algebra and statistics contribute related scientific-computing methods and are each aligned once elsewhere. No one unallocated UCR course implements this combined Python, Monte Carlo, fitting, PCA and Fourier workflow; the independent external credit remains visible.
The external course develops electronic circuits, instrumentation and measurement; general wave/material laboratories do not establish that instrumental-design inquiry.
Ethics and genetic-testing questions occur within biological courses, but their credits are already represented. No separate dedicated science/technology/society credit is invented.

UCR wave foundations and digital image analysis are substantive shared preparation. The strongest image-analysis course is aligned once with Imaging 2; this independent optical image-formation, lens/microscope and introductory imaging requirement remains visible without duplicating UCR credit.
The external unit investigates nanoscale technology and associated tools. General material/wave foundations and biological methods do not establish a separately organised nanotechnology unit.

Thermodynamic and material foundations are present, but the external statistical-thermodynamic, polymer/condensate, self-organisation and reaction-diffusion inquiry is not separately implemented in the selected courses.
Ethics and scientific communication occur within biological study, but those credits are already represented. The independent external science/technology/society unit is preserved.
The approved 30-EC minor remains genuine open space; no specialised minor contents are assumed to improve correspondence.

The compulsory 20-EC bachelor project retains its credit and entry/supervision requirements. Standard optional UCR independent research is comparison-only and does not acquire the external credit weight.

Genetics, disease and statistical learning provide related foundations, already represented once. A course organised specifically around GWAS, functional variant interpretation and polygenic risk prediction is not established by the selected UCR content.

notes.text: The UCR programmes combine molecular and cellular biology, laboratory work and quantitative methods. The first adds evolution and physical/chemical foundations; the second gives more weight to disease, immunity and biological function. Specialist nanoscale biophysics, microscopy acquisition, electronic instruments and soft-matter training remain limitations. These are related academic programmes rather than full Nanobiology equivalence.

audience.programmeDescription: Nanobiology is an English-taught joint bachelor from TU Delft and Erasmus University Rotterdam. It combines biology, physics and mathematics to investigate living systems at small scales, with laboratory, computational and imaging work. A minor, electives and a final research project complete the programme.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The first UCR programme studies living systems through molecular and laboratory biology, evolution, quantitative methods and physical foundations. The second emphasises disease, immunity and organ-system function. Delft and Erasmus provide more specialised nanoscale biophysics, microscopy and instrumentation.
